newsitem.title: FRANCE: French coffee roaster KJS raised retail prices.
newsitem.headline: French coffee roaster KJS raised retail prices.

text.p: French coffee roaster Kraft Jacob Suchard (KJS) said on Wednesday that it had raised retail prices of its roasted arabica coffee by nine francs per kilo, effective February 24.
"The rise for arabica coffee was of nine francs on February 24," Roland Monica, director general of the beverage division, told Reuters.
Industry sources said early last month that the company planned to raise retail prices for its arabicas by four francs per kilo.
Monica explained that the company, part of Philip Morris, had initially targeted a four-franc rise but decided on a nine-franc to help offset higher green coffee prices and a firmer dollar.
Kraft Jacobs Suchard has a 42 percent share of the French coffee market.

Asked if further retail price hikes were in the pipeline on the back of a fresh rally in world coffee prices, Monica said "I don't know". "I do not understand the market any more. It just went crazy," he added.
But he also warned that further rises in retail prices may eventually hurt coffee consumption.
French coffee consumption rose by around two percent in 1996, after falling by an average five percent in 1995 and 1994.
Prospects of tight supplies are cited as the main reason behind the rally that has sent arabica prices at their highest levels since the last big frost scare in Brazil two years ago.
The New York futures contract for May arabicas opened at a new contract high of over $2.00 per lb on Wednesday.
